survey: An arched blue plank door set into an orange wooden frame in a cream wall, with ivy at the sides and a stone threshold below. The camera faces the door straight on at about mid-door height. The door faces the camera squarely: its planks and the four lower panels are vertical, equal in width and evenly spaced, correct for a flat face seen front-on, and the panel rails run horizontally, parallel to the door's top and bottom edges. The frame's side posts stand vertical, the arch is symmetric and the plinth blocks sit square on the ground; the frame shows only a slight sliver of its inner side, which fits a near-frontal view. The doorknob's backplate is flat against the door and the knob is a front-facing sphere; the hinges are flush with the left edge. The wreath and bow hang flat on the door's face and are seen front-on. The threshold stones are seen slightly from above, matching an eye level around the middle of the door, and the door's bottom edge rests level on the step. In the tool marks, vertical edges (red, about 94°) and horizontal edges (blue, about 5°) form two consistent families at right angles. All planks, panel stiles, the door edge and the jamb share the red family; all rails, the threshold and the plinth tops share the blue family. The small tilt is common to the whole picture, so it reads as one camera. No round part conflicts with its surface.
